chunks: From him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces his wife with one or two divorces, then leaves her until her waiting period expires; what is her status?
He said: 'If he left her with the intention that he does not want her, she becomes definitively divorced from him and does not become permissible to him until she marries another husband.'
And if he left her with the intention that he wants to remarry her, and then a year passed for that purpose, then he is more entitled to her revocation (of the divorce).'

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: she becomes definitively divorced from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband divorces his wife once or twice and then waits for her iddah to expire without revoking the divorce?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim clarifies the distinction between a revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorce based on the husband's intent during the waiting period (iddah). It establishes that if he remains silent with the intention of revocation, the right persists for a year, whereas silence with the intention of finality renders the divorce absolute, requiring a new marriage contract (nikah) for reinstatement. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on intention (niyyah) in determining the legal status of the marital bond.
